title: Concise ops sparring cards for SE (WIP)
content:
Purpose / sprint goal:
- Create a single-sheet, rapid-reference set of "sparring" cards SEs can use in 1:1s and pilot kickoffs.
- Focus: fast technical qualification + an escalation/fallback script when customers hit latency/cost/regulatory objections.

Audience & when to use:
- Primary: Sales Engineers (platform sellers, integrators). Secondary: field SE+AE pairs during pilots.
- Use during: 15–30 min discovery, pilot planning call, pre-demo prep, emergency fallbacks in customer calls.

High-level narrative (30s):
- "Redwood gives you consistent inference economics across hosted, dedicated, and private modes — so your latency and unit-cost goals stay predictable as usage scales. When capacity or compliance limits bite, we have safe fallbacks and a canary plan so your app keeps serving."

One-liners (for different buyer angles)
- For platform engineers: "Pin model versions and rollout policies across environments — same API, less ops drift."
- For procurement/CFO: "Reserved capacity + intelligent batching typically reduces per-token cost by 20–45% vs on-demand clouds for sustained workloads."
- For security/compliance: "Private control plane and KMS integrations — audit logs and on-prem options where required."

Top 4 qualification signals to surface fast:
1) Expected qps and P95 latency targets (example: 200 qps, 150ms P95).
2) Sensitive data / compliance needs (PII, HITRUST, financial messages).
3) Burstiness profile (steady vs spiky) — affects batching & reserved capacity fit.
4) Model freshness and rollout needs (can they tolerate model fallbacks?).

Quick demo script (3 mins):
- 60s: Show API call + latency numbers against a 512 token prompt (hosted).
- 60s: Toggle routing -> dedicated pool -> show throughput dashboard (tokens/sec + token-cost).
- 60s: Show fallback: route to smaller/quantized variant + automatic prefix cache hit — demonstrate degraded-but-stable output.

Objections & sharp rebuttals (sparring-ready)
- "Your latency is inconsistent." -> "We expose per-route P95 and token-level breakdowns; if you need predictable tail latency, Dedicated + pinning + autoscale policies guarantees throughput and we instrument fallbacks to avoid outages."
- "We can't commit to reserved capacity yet." -> "Start hosted with quotas + burst routing, run a 30-day onramp and measure sustained qps. If sustained demand > X we recommend trial dedicated pool — we provide migration templates and a cost sim."
- "Model quality drops when you quantize." -> "Recommend A/B with Redwood Optimize: suggested quantization profiles per workload plus eval hooks to monitor regressions. We gate rollouts with canaries and perf thresholds."

Three-tier fallback play (scriptable steps)
- Tier A (fast): Route to compatible hosted variant in same region (0 config). Not ideal if soft-realtime desired, but instant.
- Tier B (affordable): Route to quantized/dense-optimized variant pinned to Dedicated pool (requires pre-provisioning). Lower cost, slightly higher latency in some prompts.
- Tier C (compliant): Route to Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for regulated accounts — has longest lead time but strongest guarantees.

Canary checklist (for pilots) — 8 quick checks
- [ ] Baseline token-cost + P95 from existing workload (30 min test harness).
- [ ] Prepare small canary dataset (50 prompts) that reflects worst-case length/complexity.
- [ ] Configure A/B route with explicit rollout % and rollback trigger (error rate > 2% or quality drop per eval).
- [ ] Enable prefix/KV caching for repetitive prompts.
- [ ] Set autoscale/burst thresholds and alerting channel (Slack + PagerDuty).
- [ ] Document fallback Tier mapping for the account (A/B/C).
- [ ] Confirm compliance checklist (audit logs, KMS, IP allowlist).
- [ ] Run 1 failover simulation with SE + SRE present.

Quick numbers and heuristics (cheat metrics)
- Rule of thumb: batching helps if avg request size < 300ms compute; target batching window <= 30ms for latency-sensitive apps.
- Quantization trade: expect 15–40% token-cost reduction; monitor evals for semantic drift.
- Reserved commit threshold: sustained baseline > 50% of Dedicated pool instance yields best economics.

Playbook micro-cards (for quick copy into Slack)
- "If latency spikes: check region routing first -> cache hit rate -> Dedicated pool usage -> enable fallback Tier A."
- "If cost > forecast: check batching config, cache ratios, and model variant quantization; propose Optimize-enabled config + cost sim."

Open questions / areas for product follow-up (notes)
- Need a single-pane template in Console for Tier mapping per account (A/B/C) — product ticket? (JIRA-ENG-7182)
- Auto-generated short demo snippets (30s) that SEs can paste into a recording for customers.
- Would a "fallback play button" in Console that simulates Tier A/B failover be feasible?

Risks & mitigation in-field
- Risk: SE promises instant Dedicated ramp without pre-provisioning -> Mitigate: always call out lead time and verify pool capacity on baseline call.
- Risk: quantization causes silent quality regression -> Mitigate: require eval suite + rollback gates before enabling in prod.

Next steps (immediate)
- Share this doc with field SEs for a 1-week trial; collect top 3 missing micro-cards. (Owner: Samira)
- Create a 1-pager "SE rapid-sparring cheat" (one sheet PDF) for handout at next all-hands. (Owner: Priya)
- File product request: in-console Tier mapping + failover sim. (Linked: JIRA-ENG-7182)

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Could we include tiny sequence diagrams for fallback wiring? (co-design with infra)
- Maybe an "economics quick-sim" micro-app that plugs in qps/avg tokens and spits out hosted vs dedicated estimates.
- Add short roleplay scripts (AE/SE) for different personas next iter.

-- end of draft --
